note: Upstream issue text for the lead to file on alchemy-run/alchemy (not filed here). Title: "cloudflare-runtime: Node Workerd spawns with node:child_process directly, so it cannot be given a ChildProcessSpawner". Body: "In @alchemy.run/cloudflare-runtime 2.0.0-beta.85, Docker reads Effect's ChildProcessSpawner from the context, but Node's Workerd (dist/core/node/workerd/Workerd.mjs, makeNode) calls node:child_process.spawn directly and WorkerdLive is a Layer.sync with no requirement. So a caller cannot stand workerd's spawn in for a test, or watch each child's exit, the way it can for Docker. Proposal: makeNode reads ChildProcessSpawner and spawns ChildProcess.make(command, args, { env, extendEnv: false, detached: false, killSignal: 'SIGKILL', additionalFds: { fd3: { type: 'output' } } }), reading the control pipe with handle.getOutputFd(3); WorkerdLive becomes Layer.effect and requires ChildProcessSpawner, which RuntimeServices' layerRuntime already requires through DockerLive. One gap on Effect's side: a signalled exit reaches the handle only as a failed exitCode whose cause message names the signal, so WorkerdExit.signal has to be read from that message." Three things differ from the old Node spawn and a reviewer should weigh them: the scope that served workerd now waits for workerd's exit before it closes (Effect's spawner release), not only sends SIGKILL; a startup error is classified from the last 4096 characters of stderr, not all of it; and the installed package's src/core/workerd/Workerd.ts is not changed to match dist (the old patch kept src in step; only dist runs). The plan's B3 plant reason did not hold: the shutdown property is what goes red; the two instances on one held port stayed green, because the law's spawner never reached workerd (see why) and the patched Workerd's scope waits for workerd's exit itself. One full run of the B3 file, before the spawns check was added, was red on the two real-instance laws after about 72 seconds each, with no error captured, while the shared box was under memory pressure from other sessions; six other runs of the same code were green. Its cause was not found. The plan said the lockfile change is 1 line; pnpm writes the patch hash in 5 places, so it is 10 lines of diff. No vi lock block was written (laptop lead's ruling).
